why: Cell i can only be reached from i - 1 or from i - p for a prime p ending in 3, so best[i] = cell[i] + max(best[i-1], best[i-p]): a 1-D DP over the row, with a sieve to list the allowed jumps.
hints: Think backwards: what are the possible last moves into cell i?
From i - 1, or from i - p where p is a prime with last digit 3 (3, 13, 23, 43, ...). Take the best score of those sources plus cell[i].
Sieve primes up to n - 1 and keep those ending in 3; dp left to right. O(n * J) where J is the number of such primes (about 1/4 of primes up to n).
pitfalls: Cell values can be negative; initialise with negative infinity, not 0.
Only primes ending in 3 count (3, 13, 23...), not every prime.
Cell 0 contributes 0 and the score includes the final cell.
constraints: • Bounds are not stated in the source. Assume 1 <= n <= 10^4 and -10^4 <= cell[i] <= 10^4, with cell[0] = 0.
